FAQ

  • The most common elevator technologies include traction elevators, MRL (Machine Room-Less) elevators, and hydraulic elevators. Depending on the application, there are also residential, commercial, hospital, industrial, construction, low-rise, mid-rise, and high-rise elevator systems designed for different building requirements.

  • Residential buildings typically use traction, MRL, or hydraulic elevators, depending on the number of floors, available space, and budget. Machine Room-Less elevators have become increasingly popular because they save space while offering smooth, energy-efficient operation.

  • A hydraulic elevator uses a piston and hydraulic fluid to move the cabin, making it suitable for low-rise buildings. A traction elevator uses ropes or belts with a motor and counterweight, allowing higher speeds, greater travel distances, and better energy efficiency for mid-rise and high-rise buildings.

  • Traction elevators are generally the preferred choice for high-rise buildings because they support higher speeds, longer travel distances, greater passenger capacity, and advanced traffic management systems that improve people flow.

  • Modern elevators include emergency braking systems, door sensors, backup power, load monitoring, emergency communication devices, predictive maintenance technology, and intelligent monitoring systems that help improve passenger safety and operational reliability.

  • An MRL (Machine Room-Less) elevator is a traction elevator that does not require a separate machine room. It is popular because it saves valuable building space, improves energy efficiency, reduces construction requirements, and offers reliable performance for both residential and commercial projects.

  • Modern buildings can choose from several premium elevator designs, including Glass (Panoramic) Elevators, Observation Elevators, Scenic Elevators, Luxury Elevators, and Capsule Elevators. These elevators combine functionality with aesthetics, offering panoramic views, premium cabin finishes, and distinctive architectural appeal while enhancing the overall passenger experience.
